question: Which radioactive element with atomic number 43 in the modern periodic table is unstable, and the half - lives of all its isotopes are relatively short, from 4.2 million years to 5.0 s?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Technetium__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **radioactive** **element** with atomic number 43 in the modern periodic table is Technetium (Tc). It is unstable, and all its isotopes have relatively short half-lives, ranging from 4.2 million years to 5.0 seconds. Therefore, the correct answer is option 4: Technetium.
 
• Technetium does not have any **stable** **isotopes**, making all of its isotopes radioactive. It is typically produced artificially in **nuclear** **reactors** or particle accelerators and has applications in various fields, including medicine and industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The periodic table was firstly created by** Dmitri Mendeleev.**
 
• **Henry** **Moseley** presented a revised form of the periodic table, which is known as **The** **Modern** **Periodic** **table.**
 
• **Radioactive** **elements** are an unstable form of elements in an atomic nucleus with an excess nuclear charge, which will produce a spontaneous release of radiation. The four common radioactive elements are **uranium**, **radium**, **polonium**, and **thorium**.
